transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?
I don’t enjoy my job or any of the things I used to love doing anymore, and it’s been like this for weeks. I just feel completely flat and disconnected from everything.
Have you experienced similar periods of feeling this way in the past, or is this the first time you have felt like this?

No, this isn't the first time. Looking back, these big swings between highly revved-up periods and these long, heavy downturns have actually been happening off and on for several years. It's not just something that started with this recent product relaunch.
During those revved-up periods you mentioned, did you feel unusually energetic, need much less sleep than usual, or find yourself acting in ways that were impulsive or out of character for you?

Yes, I felt incredibly energetic and buzzing, often staying up until midnight sketching out new ideas because I couldn't sit still and signed up for way too many extra projects. I also became really irritable and would snap at my husband and coworkers over tiny things, which was very out of character for me. I don't know if I actually needed less sleep, but I was definitely staying up very late working because of that constant push to keep going.
During those highly energetic periods, did you ever feel so out of control that you required hospitalization or were unable to function in your daily life at work or home?

No, I've never been hospitalized, and it actually felt like the opposite—I felt like I was functioning at 200%, taking on tons of extra projects and getting praise from my managers. Even though I was distracted and buzzing with way too much energy, I didn't experience any real breakdown in my functioning until these low periods hit.

During these heavy, low periods you described, have you ever felt so deeply depressed that you were unable to get out of bed, take care of basic needs, or continue functioning at work for at least two weeks?

Yes, this current low period has been dragging on for about six months now, which is much longer than two weeks. While I still manage to drag myself to work, my body feels like it's moving through molasses and my performance reviews have slipped because I'm missing deadlines. At home, I've been bailing on chores so much that my husband has had to pick up almost all the slack.
During these long, heavy downturns, have you ever felt that life was not worth living, or have you had any thoughts of harming yourself?

To be honest, there are nights when I lie in bed thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up in the morning. On the really rough days, I've even idly wondered how I could make it look like an accident. But I want to be clear that I haven't actually made any plans or done anything to act on those thoughts.
During these six months of feeling low, have you experienced other symptoms like significant changes in your appetite, weight, or excessive feelings of worthlessness or guilt?

I haven't noticed any major changes in my appetite or weight, but I constantly feel this overwhelming guilt, like I'm letting my team down after the relaunch and being a burden to my husband. I keep telling myself that I'm screwing everything up and that I don't really deserve any of the praise or promotions I've received.

During these six months, have you experienced any periods where you were completely unable to function at work or perform basic self-care, or have you been able to maintain at least a minimal level of daily activity throughout?

I haven't been completely bedridden, but my ability to function has definitely declined. I still go to work, but I'm moving like I'm in molasses, missing deadlines, and my manager has started asking if I'm okay. At home, I've been bailing on chores and social plans so much that my husband has had to take over almost all the daily responsibilities.
During these six months of feeling low, have there been any days where you were completely unable to get out of bed or perform basic tasks like showering or eating?

No, I haven't had days where I was completely unable to get out of bed or do basic self-care like showering. But doing absolutely anything, even the smallest task, still feels like it takes an immense amount of physical and mental effort.
